messages:
sam: Heads-up — saw a ~50% NCCL bandwidth regression on the p4 fleet in us-west-2 after yesterday's kernel + OFED bump. Appears correlated with nodes that picked up the new ofed-6.9 package. :eyes:
jen: Ugh. Which kernel and driver versions exactly?
michael: Kernel 5.15.112, nvidia-driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.1 on the affected nodes. OFED 6.9 from our repo.
sam: Right. Quick summary from `dmesg` and `ibv_devinfo` on one node:
```
[  12.345678] efa: EFA NIC ifindex 4 up
[  12.345690] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: firmware: failed to load FW image
ibv_devinfo: device 'mlx5_1' port 1: link up, mtu 4096 -> then falls back to 1500
```
raj: Falling back to 1500? That'll wreck NCCL with GPUDirect RDMA and SRQs. Any SRQ errors in logs?
sam: Yes, multiple lines like `EFA SRQ error: rcv_wr=0x... failed with -22` and `IB QP attr change failed`. Also saw `rdma_link_layer: InfiniBand` then later `Ethernet` on same link during netdev rebind.
jen: Did the ofed package change the default MTU negotiation/auto-sense settings? We recently added `rdma-core` helpers that toggle `netdev` when firmware version mismatches.
michael: I ran `ib_read_bw` and `ib_send_bw` — raw IB tests show ~12Gb/s, expected ~100Gb/s. But `nccl-tests` throughput drops and shows bad GPU-to-GPU RDMA fallbacks to TCP.
raj: Sounds like the EFA driver is losing the RDMA transport and falling back to sockets. Could be a GID/GID index mismatch after the firmware upgrade. Any changes in `ibv_devinfo -vv` for GIDs?
sam: On one node, GID index 0 was missing on port 1 until I manually toggled the `mlx5_core` module. After reload, kernel shows correct GID and MTU 4096. Bandwidth returns. But other nodes still flaky.
jen: Is there a config drift? We rolled the kernel + ofed via the same automation. Maybe some nodes didn't get the microcode/firmware blob due to failed `fwupd` step.
infra-bot: deployment-operator: rolling-updates/us-west-2 completed for group p4-large at 2026-03-17T10:21:00Z (some nodes failed post-install tests).
michael: I pulled one failed node's `dmesg` — it shows `fwloader: failed to apply fw image: -5` then `mlx5_core: License check failed` which is odd.
raj: License check? Could be our firmware package mismatch (we had two variants for 5.15 vs 5.19 kernels). If the wrong firmware is loaded, the NICs will reconfigure to a fallback path and RDMA may be disabled.
sam: Proposed immediate mitigation: rollback OFED on a canary subset (20 nodes), then monitor NCCL and `ib_*` tests. If rollback restores MTU/GID and bandwidth, escalate to vendor.
jen: Agreed. Also add a healthcheck to our rollout that runs `nccl-tests --all-gpus` and `ib_read_bw` after OFED install. Right now our post-upgrade smoke only checks `nvidia-smi`.
michael: Forensics: capture `ethtool -i ethX`, `ibv_devinfo -vv`, `dmesg`, `lsmod | grep mlx5` and `modinfo mlx5_core` before we touch anything. I scripted a collector.
raj: I'll open a ticket with the OFED vendor with the logs and mention MTU negotiation/GID loss + firmware mismatch suspicion. Also ask for guidance on which fw blobs are compatible with kernel 5.15 + driver 535.
sam: Quick note: this is impacting our reserved capacity customers in us-west-2 only. Paging account team in case we need to pro-rate credits.
jen: I'll gate further OFED upgrades in other regions until we confirm root cause.
infra-bot: rolling-update: rollback started for group p4-large-canary (20 nodes) at 2026-03-17T10:35:00Z.
sam: After rollback on first 5 nodes, `nccl-tests` bandwidth jumped back to expected numbers and `ib_read_bw` shows ~95Gb/s. Looks like rollback helps.
michael: Ok record that as temporary mitigation. Next: 1) hard-fail the fw package mismatch in our deployer 2) add RDMA smoke to postinstall 3) coordinate with vendor for firmware matrix 4) schedule full rollback or patch rollout depending on vendor response.
raj: Also check kernel versions on nodes that did not suffer the regression — maybe some nodes got a different kernel minor release that included a mlx5 fix.
sam: Good catch. I'll diff the /boot/ entries across healthy vs broken nodes.
jen: I'll put a short Status update to #incidents and tag the affected accounts. Keep replies here for technical notes. :thumbsup:
